candidate_relations.reason: Scaly thick eyelids, ectropion, and crusted margins during TNF inhibition exceed an isolated dry-eye syndrome.
No facial rosacea, telangiectasia, or meibomian pattern was reported in this 15-year-old.
Crusty plaques and erythematous thickened lids establish blepharitis but omit ectropion and its medication trigger.
The eruption tracked TNF-α inhibitors and resolved after discontinuation without evidence of rosacea.
Both lower lids were ectropic, but this finding alone omits the inflammatory drug-induced cause.
Resolution after stopping TNF inhibitors supports drug-induced eye disease, though the specific blepharitis-ectropion phenotype is missing.
Crohn disease supplies autoimmune context but the eyelid eruption appeared during biologic therapy.
Scaly lids and conjunctival hyperemia fit blepharoconjunctivitis but do not retain ectropion or TNF-inhibitor causation.
Blepharitis occurred during infliximab exposure, yet the complete case also implicates adalimumab and includes ectropion.
Symptoms recurred after adalimumab dosing, but this label omits the earlier infliximab association and lid malposition.
No dry mouth, tear deficiency testing, or systemic Sjögren evidence was provided.
Scaly periocular plaques during two TNF inhibitors fit a cutaneous drug reaction but underspecify ocular findings.
Adalimumab was temporally involved, while the broad inflammation label omits blepharitis, ectropion, and infliximab.
Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia accompanied the lid disease but is only one examination finding.
Scaly plaques can appear psoriasiform, but no psoriasis histology or extraocular eruption established that subtype.
Drug-induced blepharitis captures the core adverse reaction but leaves out ectropion and the specific TNF-α agents.
Biopsy-proven Crohn disease explains the biologic indication, not the new eyelid pathology.
The patient had Crohn disease, not autoimmune enteropathy, and neither diagnosis names the ocular adverse effect.
No atopic dermatitis history, severe pruritus, or corneal involvement supported atopic keratoconjunctivitis.
Infliximab preceded an ocular inflammatory episode, but the candidate omits adalimumab recurrence and ectropion.
